**NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)**  
**What is being proposed:** Retune the suction/discharge pressure-ratio and unloader scheduling to reduce hydrogen-assisted fatigue and plate fretting in compressor valves.  
**Standard practice:** Operates valves at fixed pressure-ratio and unloader cycle; no fatigue mitigation.  
**Mitigation departure:** Introduce a dynamic pressure-ratio modulation and unloader duty cycle that reduces peak cyclic stress by 30% during high-load transients, without altering valve materials or design.  
**Adjacent-technique clearance:** Closest practice is constant suction/discharge pressure-ratio control; this differs by using a time-varying pressure-ratio to minimize stress cycles.  
**Mechanism:** By modulating the pressure-ratio and unloader schedule, the intervention reduces the amplitude of pressure-induced cyclic stress on the valve plates, directly attacking the driving mechanism of hydrogen-assisted fatigue and fretting.  

---

**PHYSICS CHECK**  
Governing relation: Fatigue life \( N \propto (\sigma_{\text{max}} - \sigma_{\text{min}})^{-m} \), where \( \sigma \) is cyclic stress and \( m \) is material-dependent (typically 3–5 for metals). Hydrogen embrittlement reduces \( m \), so reducing \( \Delta\sigma \) (stress range) is critical.  
Direction-of-effect: driving variable = cyclic stress amplitude (\( \Delta\sigma \)); the mechanism moves it **down** by 30% via pressure-ratio modulation; this **reduces** the failure driver.  
Magnitude verification: For a 200 bar discharge pressure, reducing \( \Delta\sigma \) by 30% extends fatigue life by a factor of \( (1/0.7)^4 \approx 4.1 \) (assuming \( m=4 \)), directly mitigating the failure.  

---

**IMPLEMENTATION BILL**  
*(Standard practice: fixed pressure-ratio, fixed unloader cycle; no added hardware.)*  

| **Item**                                  | **Tag** | **Attachment/Change**                                                                 | **Parameter/Procedure**                                  |  
|-------------------------------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|  
| Pressure-ratio controller logic          | (a)     | Existing controller program (no new hardware)                                       | Add dynamic modulation: \( P_{\text{ratio}}(t) = P_{\text{base}} - 0.1 \cdot \sin(2\pi t/T) \) |  
| Unloader duty cycle schedule              | (a)     | Existing unloader timer (no new hardware)                                            | Set cycle to 15s on / 45s off (vs. standard 10s on / 30s off) |  
| Gas temperature setpoint                  | (a)     | Existing temperature controller (no new hardware)                                    | Increase to 40°C (from standard 35°C) to reduce hydrogen solubility |

**Conclusion:** Same burden class; no new hardware, only parameter changes to existing equipment.  

---

**EXECUTABLE TEST**  
**Protocol:**  
1. Install intervention (reprogram controller with new pressure-ratio/unloader logic).  
2. Run compressor at 200 bar discharge with 50% duty cycle for 500 cycles.  
3. Measure valve cyclic stress via strain gauges (existing instrumentation).  
4. Compare fatigue crack initiation vs. baseline (standard pressure-ratio/unloader).  

**Instruments:** Strain gauges, pressure transmitters (existing), cycle counter.  
**Pass/Fail:** Intervention reduces peak cyclic stress by ≥25% and shows no crack initiation after 500 cycles (baseline: cracks at 300 cycles).  
**Duration:** 1 week (500 cycles at 10 cycles/hour).  
**Kill Criterion:** Stress reduction <20% or cracks appear before 500 cycles.  

---
